title: Policies for Information Security
description: Specifies that organizations must have an information security policy document in place. This is to protect themselves against information security threats.

title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
description: Emphasizing the importance of clearly defined and documented information security roles and responsibilities to ensure accountability and effective management across an organization.

title: Segregation of Duties
description: Emphasizes segregating duties to reduce risks like fraud and errors by clearly defining and separating roles.

title: Management Responsibilities
description: Emphasizes management's responsibility to enforce information security by ensuring employees and contractors are informed, trained, and compliant with security policies, while also allocating resources and providing channels for reporting violations.

title: Contact With Authorities
description: Specifies that an organization should maintain a process for contacting the appropriate authorities per its legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.

title: Contact With Special Interest Groups
description: The need for organizations to engage with special interest groups and professional associations to stay updated on security best practices, threats, and expert advice.

title: Threat Intelligence
description: Emphasizing the need for organizations to gather, analyze, and act on threat data to strengthen information security through actionable insights and periodic assessments

title: Information Security in Project Management
description: Integrates information security into project management by identifying risks early, implementing controls throughout the project lifecycle, and ensuring compliance with ISO standards

title: Inventory of Information and Other Associated Assets
description: Mandates creating and maintaining an inventory of information assets to enhance security, risk management, and compliance

title: Acceptable Use of Information and Other Associated Assets
description: Emphasizing the creation and enforcement of acceptable use policies to safeguard information and assets, ensuring compliance, and mitigating risks like unauthorized access or data breaches.

title: Return of Assets
description: Emphasizing the secure return of organizational assets when roles or contracts end, to prevent data breaches and ensure compliance with information security policies.

title: Classification of Information
description: Focusing on classifying information by sensitivity and criticality to ensure proper protection and compliance with security standards. It highlights key steps like defining classifications, training staff, and monitoring compliance.

title: Labelling of Information
description: Requires organizations to label information assets based on their classification to enhance security and streamline management, emphasizing the use of metadata for digital assets and clear procedures for labelling.

title: Access Control
description: Implementing tailored access control policies to ensure secure, role-based, and least-privilege access to organizational assets, using both technological and physical measures to mitigate risks.

title: Identity Management
description: Highlighting best practices for secure identity management, access control, and compliance to protect systems and data from unauthorized access.

title: Authentication Information
description: Highlighting the secure management of authentication data (passwords, tokens, biometrics) through encryption, secure transmission, and regular updates to prevent unauthorized access and ensure compliance with information security standards.

title: Access Rights
description: Focusing on managing access rights by ensuring proper authorization, segregation of duties, timely revocation, and regular reviews to protect information systems and align with business needs.

title: Information Security in Supplier Relationships
description: Emphasizing the management of information security risks in supplier relationships through due diligence, clear agreements, ongoing monitoring, and tailored policies to ensure compliance and data protection.

title: Addressing Information Security Within Supplier Agreements
description: Emphasizes establishing clear information security obligations within supplier agreements to mitigate risks, including access controls, audits, and compliance measures.

title: Managing Information Security in the ICT Supply Chain
description: Focusing on managing information security risks in the ICT supply chain by establishing security standards, ensuring supplier compliance, and verifying secure delivery of ICT components. It highlights governance integration and supplier accountability for security.

title: Monitoring, Review and Change Management of Supplier Services
description: Emphasizes monitoring, reviewing, and managing changes in supplier services to maintain agreed levels of information security, tailoring actions to the criticality of risks and fostering compliance through structured policies and senior oversight.

title: Information Security for Use of Cloud Services
description: Focuses on ensuring the secure use of cloud services through defined security requirements, roles, provider selection criteria, control allocation, and incident management, emphasizing tailored policies and exit strategies for organizations.

title: Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation
description: Focusing on planning and preparing for information security incident management through standardized reporting, effective response processes, trained personnel, and continuous improvement to enhance organizational resilience.

title: Assessment and Decision on Information Security Events
description: Focusing on assessing information security events to determine if they qualify as incidents, ensuring effective prioritization and management of potential threats.

title: Response to Information Security Incidents
description: Focusing on managing information security incidents through effective processes, including containment, mitigation, and evidence handling, with ownership assigned to senior management for oversight.

title: Learning From Information Security Incidents
description: Focuses on learning from information security incidents through documentation, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent recurrence and enhance security measures.

title: Collection of Evidence
description: Outlines procedures for systematically collecting and preserving evidence during information security incidents to meet legal and disciplinary requirements, emphasizing integrity, legality, and proper handling.

title: Information Security During Disruption
description: Focuses on ensuring information security during business disruptions by maintaining, adapting, and compensating for security controls as part of continuity plans to prevent data breaches and uphold integrity​​.

title: ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
description: Ensures organizations maintain readiness for business continuity by identifying critical activities, implementing structured response plans, and regularly testing and updating them to ensure resilience during disruptions.

title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Requirements
description: Requires organizations to identify, document, and comply with all legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations related to information security, integrating them into policies, risk assessments, and supplier management.

title: Intellectual Property Rights
description: Emphasizing the importance of complying with intellectual property (IP) rights for software and assets, detailing practices like sourcing software responsibly, maintaining asset registers, and adhering to licensing terms to avoid legal or financial consequences.

title: Protection of Records
description: Focuses on protecting organizational records from loss, damage, unauthorized access, and destruction by implementing policies for secure handling, retention, classification, and disposal while ensuring compliance with legal and business requirements.

title: Privacy and Protection of PII
description: Preventive measure that helps keep risk at bay, through the production of guidelines and procedures that meet the legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations of an organization with respect to the storage, privacy and protection of Personal Identifiable Information (PII) in all its forms.

title: Independent Review of Information Security
description: Emphasizing the requirement for organizations to periodically conduct independent reviews of their information security to ensure compliance, identify gaps, and improve security measures.

title: Compliance With Policies, Rules and Standards for Information Security
description: Requires organizations to ensure compliance with internal information security policies, assign oversight responsibilities, and implement corrective actions to maintain a strong security posture.

title: Documented Operating Procedures
description: Emphasizing the need for documented operating procedures to ensure secure, consistent, and efficient information security operations, particularly for critical, infrequent, or high-risk activities.

title: Screening
description: Mandates organizations to conduct appropriate background checks on employees and suppliers before granting them access to sensitive information, ensuring trustworthiness and compliance with legal and security standards.

title: Terms and Conditions of Employment
description: Need for organizations to define employees' information security responsibilities in their terms of employment, including confidentiality agreements, legal obligations, and consequences for security breaches.

title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training
description: Emphasizes the need for organizations to implement ongoing information security awareness, education, and training programs to ensure employees understand and fulfil their security responsibilities. It aligns with previous standards while adding clarity and structured guidance for better compliance.

title: Disciplinary Process
description: Need for organizations to implement a formal disciplinary process to address information security violations, ensuring clear communication, fair enforcement, and compliance with legal and organizational policies.

title: Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment
description: Explains the importance of defining and enforcing information security responsibilities that continue after employment ends or changes, ensuring data protection and access revocation to prevent security risks.

title: Confidentiality or Non-Disclosure Agreements
description: Mandates organizations to establish confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) to protect sensitive information from unauthorized disclosure. It outlines key compliance measures, including data ownership, agreement duration, monitoring, and consequences for breaches.

title: Remote Working
description: Emphasizes the importance of secure remote working by implementing access controls, physical security measures, and data protection policies to mitigate risks associated with remote environments.

title: Information Security Event Reporting
description: Outlines the importance of prompt reporting of information security events to ensure quick response and risk mitigation. It mandates organizations to establish clear reporting mechanisms, educate personnel, and document incidents to maintain security and compliance.

title: Physical Security Perimeters
description: Physical Security Perimeters ensures systematic implementation and monitoring of physical security measures, enhancing overall organizational security and regulatory compliance. Achieving compliance with ISO 27001:2022 fosters trust with stakeholders by demonstrating a commitment to safeguarding critical information assets.

title: Physical Entry
description: Focuses on securing physical entry points to sensitive areas using access controls like keypads, biometrics, and RFID systems, ensuring only authorized personnel can enter to protect information and assets.

title: Securing Offices, Rooms and Facilities
description: Focuses on securing offices, rooms, and facilities by preventing unauthorized access, protecting information assets, and reducing security risks through measures like controlled access, surveillance, and strategic facility design.

title: Physical Security Monitoring
description: Covers physical security monitoring, emphasizing CCTV, alarms, and access controls to prevent unauthorized access to restricted areas while ensuring compliance with data protection laws.

title: Protecting Against Physical and Environmental Threats
description: Mandates organizations to assess and mitigate risks from physical and environmental threats, such as natural disasters and human-induced incidents, through proactive risk assessment, security controls, and continuous monitoring to protect critical infrastructure and information assets.

title: Working In Secure Areas
description: Outlines security requirements for working in secure areas, emphasizing restricted access, supervised activities, controlled use of devices, and emergency preparedness to protect information assets from unauthorized access or misuse.

title: Clear Desk and Clear Screen
description: Emphasizes securing sensitive information by ensuring workspaces and digital screens are free from exposed data when unattended. Key measures include secure storage, device protection, user authentication, printer security, and proper disposal of sensitive materials.

title: Equipment Siting and Protection
description: Focuses on protecting equipment from physical, environmental, and unauthorized access threats through secure placement, environmental monitoring, and security controls.

title: Security of Assets Off-Premises
description: Focuses on securing information assets when used or stored off-premises, addressing risks like loss, theft, or unauthorized access. It mandates physical security, authorization procedures, remote management, and compliance with manufacturer guidelines to protect sensitive data outside the organization's premises.

title: Storage Media
description: Outlines best practices for managing storage media securely, covering policies for authorization, encryption, storage, transfer, and disposal to prevent unauthorized access, data loss, or breaches.

title: Supporting Utilities
description: Highlights the importance of protecting essential utilities (e.g., power, water, cooling, and telecoms) to prevent disruptions in information processing facilities. It provides guidance on risk mitigation through audits, redundancy, network segregation, and secure configurations to ensure business continuity.

title: Cabling Security
description: Highlights the importance of securing cabling infrastructure to prevent unauthorized access, damage, or interference. It provides guidance on protective measures such as underground placement, segregation, shielding, and access control to maintain business continuity.

title: Equipment Maintenance
description: Highlights the importance of maintaining IT equipment to protect information assets, ensuring proper procedures, authorized personnel, and security controls are in place during maintenance to prevent data breaches and operational failures.

title: Secure Disposal or Re-Use of Equipment
description: Mandates secure disposal or reuse of equipment by ensuring irreversible data removal, physical destruction of storage media, and removal of identifying labels to protect sensitive information.

title: User Endpoint Devices
description: Outlines security measures for user endpoint devices (e.g., laptops, mobile phones), emphasizing policies, access controls, encryption, and user responsibilities to protect information assets from threats like unauthorized access, loss, or theft.

title: Privileged Access Rights
description: Explains the importance of managing privileged access rights to reduce security risks. It emphasizes controlled, event-based access allocation, maintaining authorization records, and ensuring minimal access necessary for users.

title: Information Access Restriction
description: Highlights the importance of controlling access to sensitive information, ensuring only authorized users can view or modify data. It emphasizes dynamic access management, granular control, real-time monitoring, and audit logging to prevent unauthorized access or misuse.

title: Access to Source Code
description: Emphasizes strict access controls, secure storage, audit trails, and change management for source code to protect intellectual property and prevent unauthorized modifications. It replaces Annex A 9.4.5 from ISO 27001:2013 with a more structured approach to source code security.

title: Secure Authentication
description: Mandates secure authentication mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access, recommending multi-factor authentication (MFA), biometric logins, and smart access controls for enhanced security.

title: Capacity Management
description: Ensures that organizations proactively manage IT resources to meet current and future operational demands, preventing system failures and optimizing performance. The control emphasizes monitoring, stress testing, and planning for scalability to maintain business continuity.

title: Protection Against Malware
description: Focusing on protecting organizations from malware through anti-malware software, user awareness, controlled access, and robust security policies to prevent, detect, and mitigate threats.

title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities
description: Focuses on managing technical vulnerabilities by identifying risks, maintaining an asset inventory, assessing threats, and implementing mitigation measures to protect an organization's ICT infrastructure. It emphasizes proactive vulnerability management to strengthen information security.

title: Configuration Management
description: Emphasizing the need for structured policies, standardized configurations, and security controls to ensure secure and efficient IT operations. It highlights the importance of documentation, monitoring, and assigning responsibilities for managing configurations effectively.

title: Information Deletion
description: Focuses on the secure deletion of unnecessary data to prevent unauthorized disclosure, requiring organizations to use appropriate deletion methods, document activities, and ensure compliance when using third-party vendors.

title: Data Masking
description: Explains data masking as a security measure to protect sensitive information, using techniques like pseudonymization, anonymization, and encryption to prevent unauthorized access while ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

title: Data Leakage Prevention
description: Outlining strategies like data classification, monitoring, encryption, and access restrictions to mitigate unauthorized data disclosure. It emphasizes proactive security measures and compliance best practices for organizations handling sensitive information.

title: Information Backup
description: Outlines the importance of implementing secure, regularly tested backup policies to ensure data recovery and business continuity, with updates focusing on encryption, cloud backups, and enhanced reporting.

title: Redundancy of Information Processing Facilities
description: Highlights the importance of redundancy in information processing facilities to ensure availability, resilience, and business continuity by duplicating critical components and implementing failover measures.

title: Logging
description: Emphasizes the importance of logging critical system events to enhance security, detect breaches, and support investigations. It outlines key events to log, best practices for log protection, and the need for regular monitoring to ensure data integrity and compliance.

title: Monitoring Activities
description: Highlights the need for organizations to proactively and reactively monitor IT and security operations to prevent incidents, detect anomalies, and ensure compliance. It outlines key monitoring areas, recommended tools, and supporting controls for effective cybersecurity risk management.

title: Clock Synchronization
description: Emphasizes the importance of synchronizing system clocks to ensure accurate data logging, effective incident monitoring, and compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. Organizations should use reliable time sources, such as NTP or PTP, and establish redundancy to maintain consistency across systems.

title: Use of Privileged Utility Programs
description: Outlines guidelines for managing privileged utility programs, emphasizing restricted access, authorization controls, logging, and periodic reviews to prevent security risks and maintain system integrity.

title: Installation of Software on Operational Systems
description: Outlines best practices for controlled software installation on operational systems, ensuring security, compliance, and minimizing risks through strict authorization, testing, logging, and rollback procedures.

title: Networks Security
description: focuses on network security by implementing controls to prevent unauthorized access, ensure secure data transmission, segment network traffic, and monitor activities to safeguard ICT infrastructure.

title: Security of Network Services
description: Outlines best practices for securing network services, emphasizing authentication, encryption, access controls, and monitoring to prevent unauthorized access and ensure service reliability.

title: Segregation of Networks
description: Explains the importance of network segregation to enhance security by restricting traffic flow between sub-networks. It provides guidance on network segmentation, access control, and wireless network security to prevent unauthorized access and mitigate security risks.

title: Web filtering
description: Outlines web filtering as a security measure to prevent access to malicious or inappropriate websites, reducing risks like malware infections and data breaches. It recommends blocking high-risk sites, enforcing access rules, and training staff on safe web usage.

title: Use of Cryptography
description: Mandates organizations to establish policies and procedures for cryptographic techniques to ensure data confidentiality, integrity, and security. It covers encryption standards, key management, legal considerations, and roles for implementing cryptographic controls effectively.

title: Secure Development Life Cycle
description: Outlines the requirements for integrating security throughout the software development life cycle (SDLC), ensuring secure coding, vulnerability testing, and compliance with security best practices from design to deployment.

title: Application Security Requirements
description: Outlines application security requirements, emphasizing risk assessments, trust levels, data protection, and compliance to safeguard applications against threats and unauthorized access.

title: Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles
description: Emphasizes integrating secure system architecture and engineering principles across the system lifecycle, promoting "security by design," zero trust, and defense-in-depth strategies to mitigate emerging threats.

title: Secure Coding
description: Emphasizes secure coding practices to prevent vulnerabilities, ensuring software security through proper development, implementation, and review processes. It highlights compliance responsibilities, real-world risks like the Heartbleed bug, and best practices for organizations to mitigate security threats.

title: Security Testing in Development and Acceptance
description: Mandates security testing throughout development and acceptance phases to identify vulnerabilities before deployment. It ensures compliance with security requirements through structured testing plans, in-house evaluations, and supplier oversight.

title: Outsourced Development
description: Outlines security requirements for outsourced system and software development, ensuring compliance with information security policies to mitigate risks like data breaches. Key measures include secure coding, threat modeling, contract agreements, vulnerability testing, and supplier audits.

title: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments
description: Emphasizes the importance of separating development, testing, and production environments to prevent unauthorized access, accidental changes, and security breaches. It provides best practices like access control, change management, and data protection to maintain system integrity.

title: Change Management
description: Outlines best practices for change management, ensuring that changes to information systems are planned, assessed, authorized, tested, documented, and communicated to maintain security, integrity, and compliance.

title: Test Information
description: Emphasizes protecting sensitive information in test environments by implementing access controls, data masking, and ensuring secure deletion after use to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches.

title: Protection of Information Systems During Audit Testing
description: Ensures the protection of information systems during audit testing by restricting access, enforcing read-only permissions, securing auditor devices, and maintaining audit trails to prevent unauthorized disclosure or system impact.
